# LiFePO4 vs NMC: LiFePO4 is the better choice for most people

**Cycle life is the biggest difference.**
- LiFePO4 (also called LFP) stations are typically rated for 3,000 to 6,000 cycles. NMC units are typically rated for 500 to 1,000 ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- With daily use, 500 cycles lasts about 1.4 years and 3,000 cycles about 8 years.
- Check the end point of the rating. "To 70%" promises less than "to 80%" ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

**Safety favors LiFePO4, though neither chemistry is risk-free.**
- In lab tests on small cells, LFP failed more mildly. It peaked at about 259°C versus 731°C for NMC in one study ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- One overcharge study found LFP reached thermal runaway earlier but was less violent afterward ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)).
- Some sites call LFP nearly fireproof, but the more careful sources note that LFP systems have had incidents too ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

**NMC's weight advantage is smaller than you'd expect.**
- At the cell level, NMC stores much more energy per kilogram.
- In finished stations, the gap shrinks to roughly 10 to 16% because the case, inverter, and fans weigh the same either way ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- Some LFP models are lighter per watt-hour than some NMC ones, so compare specific models.

**Price no longer favors NMC.**
- One retailer database shows a median of about $0.55 per Wh for LFP versus $0.95 for NMC ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- LFP is also far cheaper per rated cycle.

**Cold weather depends more on the brand than the chemistry.** Most stations of either type won't charge below 32°F, so check the manual.

## When NMC still makes sense
- You want the lightest possible unit and will use it rarely.
- You find a deeply discounted unit for a few weekend trips a year.
- You already own a working NMC station. There's no need to replace it.

Most major brands have moved their current lineups to LiFePO4, so if you're buying new, you'll mostly be choosing between LFP models anyway.

## One LiFePO4 example
The **BLUETTI Elite 200 V2** is a 2,073.6 Wh LiFePO4 station with a 2,600 W inverter, a 6,000-cycle rating, and a 5-year warranty. It isn't expandable. The list price is $899, and one listing says code AFF5OFF takes $44.95 off, bringing it to $854.05. Prices and codes change, so confirm at checkout.

[Buy the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2). This is an affiliate link, so the seller earns a commission if you buy through it.

Before buying any unit, check that the spec sheet says LiFePO4 or LFP, and size the capacity and inverter to what you need to run. Fit matters more than chemistry.
